sections.html:
Davie County Tax Administration has three divisions: real property appraisal (which also covers mapping and land records), personal property appraisal, and tax collection. Billing and payment belong to the collector, while listings and assessed values belong to the assessor.

The Administration Building, 123 South Main Street in Mocksville, takes listings Monday to Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM, whether you come in, file online or mail them. Reach the assessor at 336 753-6120 and revaluation staff at 336-753-6140. Appeals on real property are sent to that same address.

Thinking of selling? Ask the collector what is owed on the parcel right now, then ring the assessor if the value or an exemption on the property card looks off.

Mostly rural, Davie is gaining suburban residents: 45,855 people in July 2025, a 7.3% rise over the 42,719 of April 2020. Owner-occupied homes make up 82.2% of housing, valued at a median of $253,900 (2020-2024), and median household income is $75,057. With owners so common, the exclusions below apply to many sellers.

Davie levies $0.6486 per $100 of valuation countywide for fiscal 2026-2027, and your parcel's location adds more. Multiply the tax value by the combined rate to get the bill.

Davie County rates for the 2026-27 fiscal year
AreaRate
Davie County$0.6486 per $100 valuation
Davie County Fire Protection (countywide)$0.04 per $100 valuation
Town of Mocksville$0.29 per $100 valuation
Town of Cooleemee$0.42 per $100 valuation, plus a $75.00 solid waste fee per residence
Town of Bermuda Run$0.15 per $100 valuation, plus a $716.46 gate fee
Advance Rural Fire Protection$.02438 per $100 valuation

The county's budget guide for the same year keeps the countywide rate at 64.86 cents and the fire tax at 4 cents. On a tax bill, the countywide fire levy shows up as ADVL followed by a number. Ask the collector which fire district covers your parcel before you work out a payoff.

Expect your bill shortly after July 1. It is due September 1, but payment is taken through January 5 (the next business day when that is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday). No bill by September 15? Phone the collector.

  • Payments must arrive or be postmarked by the deadline. With no postmark, the delivery day counts, so mail at least 5 business days ahead.
  • Real estate accounts that go past due are charged 2% for January and 3/4% for each month beyond.
  • Partial payments are welcome, and a mailed one needs a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Paying online by card adds a convenience fee and requires the bill year, account number and bill number.

Between March 1 and June 30, current-year delinquent real property liens must be advertised in a newspaper, with the cost added to what the owner owes. Wage, bank account and rent garnishment, foreclosure and tax warrants are all in the collection toolkit. By statute the lien on a parcel arises on the listing date, January 1.

Values were last reset effective January 1, 2025, with notices to owners in February 2025. Before that came 2021. Davie has recently revalued every four years, though state law only requires one every eight.

County staff did the work in house. Appraisers sorted the county into roughly 215 appraisal neighborhoods, compared recent sales and applied one schedule of values. The revaluation covers near 24,000 parcels, and the schedule stays in use until a new one is needed or 8 years pass.

To contest a value:

  • Fill out the appeal form completely, sign and date it, and return it within thirty days of receiving it.
  • Send it to the Revaluation Office at 123 South Main Street, Mocksville, NC 27028, email it with supporting documents, or use the online form on the Revaluation/Land Records page.
  • State your basis for the appeal. Some appeals get a site visit.
  • Watch for a letter saying whether the value changed. It can go up, stay the same or go down.

Some sales do not count as qualified comparisons: a conveyance of two or more parcels, transactions between relatives or related businesses, undivided or fractional interests, sales involving governments, utilities, lenders or relocation firms, and forced or auction sales. Pick comparables outside those categories. Lose before the county board and you can go to the Property Tax Commission, within 30 days of the date the board's notice was mailed. Call 336-753-6140 to find out when the next appeal window opens.

Three state programs exist, and each owner picks only one:

  • Elderly and disabled exclusion: income of $39,900 or less, and a cut of $25,000 or 50% of the value of the house and one acre.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: honorable discharge and a 100% service-related disability, with no income cap, for $45,000 off the home and one acre.
  • Circuit breaker: income of $59,850 or below, North Carolina residency, and five years owning and living in the home.

Income ceilings shift from year to year, so ask the assessor for the current figures. If you already receive an exclusion you need not reapply, but the circuit breaker requires a fresh application annually. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, who must take it up to June 1 ahead of the tax year.

The circuit breaker defers any tax above the cap and records it as a lien. A sale makes up to three prior years of deferred tax payable, so find that figure before you list.

The listing window is the month of January. Forms must arrive or be postmarked by January 31, and a late listing draws a 10% penalty. Owners also report new buildings and improvements and list unregistered vehicles, mobile homes, boats and business assets.

At closing the seller usually pays the year's tax, with proration as a courtesy between the two sides. The legal duty rests with the January 1 owner of record, yet collection can follow the property to the next owner, so settle the split with your attorney.

  • Ask the collector for a payoff covering every open year and any advertised delinquency.
  • The grantor purchases the state deed stamp at the register of deeds before recording, at one dollar per five hundred dollars of price.
  • On the circuit breaker, expect the deferred amount to come due on transfer.
  • Any lien for unpaid tax must be cleared through closing, no matter who buys.

A fast cash closing can pay off delinquent taxes before newspaper advertising adds cost, and it skips the lender's appraisal, which leaves the payoff figure as the main number to settle. Give the closing attorney your latest bill and any exclusion paperwork.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Davie County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Tax Collector by mail, in person at the Administration Building, in the dropbox, or online with a card. Mailed payments can go to the lockbox, and the office has a teller window. Online card payments carry a convenience fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Davie County value?
faqs.a: Return the appeal form within thirty days of receiving it, with your basis and any documents. Call 336-753-6140 to ask when the next appeal window opens.

faqs.q: What is the Davie County tax rate in Mocksville?
faqs.a: A Mocksville parcel is charged the county rate of $0.6486 per $100, the countywide fire rate of $0.04 and the town rate of $0.29 for 2026-27. Other towns and fire districts have their own figures in the table above.

faqs.q: Must I renew a Davie County elderly exclusion each year?
faqs.a: No. An owner already receiving an exclusion does not need to reapply. The circuit breaker is different, because the state requires a new application each year.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamp on a Davie County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The register of deeds collects one dollar per five hundred dollars of price (a leftover fraction counts as another five hundred) at recording, and the proceeds are split between the county and the state.
